metaDescription: Evaluate JSON Pointers like /a/0/b or #/a%20b against a document, with ~0 and ~1 escapes and the canonical form shown. Free, in your browser.
intro: Paste a JSON document and a list of JSON Pointers to see the value each one points to, its tokens and its canonical escaped form, or the reason it fails.
why:
JSON Pointer is the addressing syntax behind JSON Schema references, OpenAPI $ref values and JSON Patch paths. It looks simple, but a few rules cause real bugs: keys that contain a slash or a tilde must be escaped, array indexes cannot have leading zeros, and the empty string points to the whole document.

Paste a document on one side and your pointers on the other, one per line, and see exactly what each resolves to. Errors name the cause, such as a missing key or an index out of range. The tool also understands URI fragment form starting with a hash and decodes percent escapes first. It evaluates pointers only and cannot modify the document.
howTo: Paste the JSON document into the first box.
Enter pointers in the second box, one per line, such as /users/0/name.
Read the value, tokens and canonical form for each pointer.

faq.q: How do I address a key containing a slash?
faq.a: Write the slash as ~1 and a tilde as ~0. The key a/b becomes /a~1b, and m~n becomes /m~0n. The tool shows the canonical escaped path for each pointer.

faq.q: What does the empty pointer mean?
faq.a: An empty string refers to the entire document, and a lone slash refers to a key that is the empty string. Both are valid and have different results.

faq.q: Is the dash token supported in arrays?
faq.a: The dash means the position after the last element and is only meaningful when adding in JSON Patch. When reading, it fails with an error, as in the standard.

faq.q: Is this the same as JSONPath?
faq.a: No. JSON Pointer addresses exactly one location with slash-separated tokens. JSONPath is a query language with wildcards and filters; use the JSONPath tester for that.
